body.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\) and fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\). If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\) and every recovered component law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\), then the pooled-law tuple identifies each labeled type graph \(D_r\). If the recovered law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), it also identifies the \(\iota\)-indexed contrast vector \(\boldsymbol\tau=((\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}))_{r=1}^{K}\) through the displayed truncated factorization at \(V_{i_X}\).
body.justification: This theorem composes unrestricted labeled-law unpooling with the published direct-law CPCM identification result, while reserving intervention effects for the stricter positive-polynomial Poisson subclass.
body.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin identifies a causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM DAG from a direct joint law and permits arbitrary source-node laws; it does not recover labeled type laws from several known-composition pools. Gao--Cai--Hara and Luo--Sun--Zhang likewise do not supply that labeled multi-composition inverse.
body.consumer: It states exactly what a successful known-composition bulk assay identifies at the cellular causal level: broad-class labeled DAGs, but polynomial-subclass intervention contrasts.
